# Task: Phase W4 — continue Phase W3 now that memory is free (zero model cost)

Read `TASK_PHASE_W.md`, `TASK_PHASE_W2.md`, `TASK_PHASE_W3.md` and `stage-s1/PHASE_W_REPORT.md`
(through `## Phase W3`). All hard rules still apply. The user closed 15 idle Claude sessions: container
memory is now ~4.6 GB of 10.7 GB (anon ~1.0 GB, the rest reclaimable file cache). Keep anonymous memory
(`anon` in `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.stat`) below ~7 GB; you may run references/audits in parallel within that.

Complete every remaining gate listed at the end of `## Phase W3` (three new offline references, all-cycle
token inventory and worst-state overhead recordings, final admission per arm with the shared measured
overhead bound, guard caps from max sessions over three seeds, frozen rules/amendment/smoke registrations
and validators, mock driver qualification with full independent audit duration/peak memory, restored
follow-on session checks, applicable launcher-stop/native negatives, prepared real commands). Do not run
any real smoke or trajectory. Append `## Phase W4` to `stage-s1/PHASE_W_REPORT.md` with exact numbers and
a clear release status (ready / blocked, and why).
I’ll read the Phase W rules and W3 gate list, complete the remaining offline work, and record the release status without running any real smoke or trajectory.

The retained results establish three completed references and a measured overhead floor of 471,000 tokens. Anonymous memory is now about 1.1 GiB. I’ll run the three missing references in fresh directories and check admission using one shared overhead bound for both arms.

The three missing references are running, and the full one-hour physical/idle audit has started on the retained d300 seed-1 run. I found that the preparatory admission script used separate per-arm overhead bounds; a new W4 version will apply the maximum measured bound to both arms and preserve the earlier script.

The d300 reference passed its independent physical audit; its idle audit is still running. Anonymous memory has fallen to about 3.2 GiB after initialization. I also prepared fresh checkpoint copies for the follow-on session checks, leaving both interrupted W2 attempts untouched.

The runtime and all auditors still match the S0 copies byte-for-byte. The prepared driver also contains a later W2 change that enforces fresh isolated test homes; I’ve recorded its exact diff. Fresh native-negative and launcher-stop checks are queued to validate that driver before release.

All three new references have completed their first scripted session without reported failures. The d300 physical audit took 23.374 seconds and peaked at 1,607,620 KiB RSS. The slower idle replay is still running; I’ll use its completed profile for the final duration and memory figures.

Anonymous memory is holding near 3.6 GiB. The references are still advancing between anchors, and the idle audit has not finished. The remaining qualification steps are queued behind admission; none can launch a real smoke or trajectory.

The retained reference profiles took roughly 78–94 minutes each, so this is likely to take several hours once mock runs and full audits are included. The active jobs are using CPU and remain within the memory limit. I’m continuing through the gates without shortening the runs or audits.
The jobs remain active with no reported failure. The final report will distinguish reference verification, independent physical/idle audits, and native mock-driver qualification.

There is enough memory headroom to run the two mock arms concurrently once admission passes. I’m also handing off the audit queue so d900 can start now while the existing d300 idle audit continues uninterrupted.
Both d300 references have reached their second decision cycle; d900 is advancing toward its next anchor. The parallel audit handoff is active, and anonymous memory remains below 5 GiB.

The references and both idle audits are still running without reported failures. Anonymous memory is about 4.7 GiB, within the ceiling.
No new gate has finished. Admission and registration freeze remain pending the complete six-reference token inventory.
The five compute jobs are still active; no failure has been reported. Memory remains steady, so no additional throttling is needed.

Both d300 references have reached cycle 3. Anonymous memory is about 4.8 GiB; no failure has been reported.
